text:
Roope Hintz is scoring like the Stars hoped he would when he was healthy. He has 21 points in 21 games, a five-game point streak, and two assists in Tuesday's comeback win in Vegas. That's well above the pace we'd expect to hold, after a 2025-26 in which he played 53 games.

Some of it is shooting: eight goals on 6.6 expected (the quality of his chances), at 21.6%, and Dallas has scored 3.3 more goals than expected with him on the ice. But the underlying play is sound. The Stars take 54% of the expected goals at five on five when he plays, and Evolving-Hockey rated him a strong defensive forward last season, with opponents creating fewer chances against him than against almost anyone (99th percentile), though they also flagged that his results ran ahead of his chances.

He's fast, with lots of bursts over 20 mph by NHL Edge, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he carries the puck in on 63% of his entries. Watch the goal pace settle; the all-around game should hold.
